title: AI is the World’s largest Relationship Therapist — Clay Cockrell & Tony Fabrikant, CoupleWork AI
talk_summary: A couples therapist and his engineer co-founder argue that general LLM assistants fail at relationship advice because sycophancy makes users more certain rather than more self-aware, and describe their product Maxine, which encodes Gottman/EFT clinical frameworks and safety-escalation protocols.

takeaways.technique: Expert-derived eval suite written TDD-style before prompting
takeaways.what_they_do: They sit with a clinician to define what 'good' looks like, then encode it as hundreds of evals written test-first, and treat that suite as the primary development tool rather than the prompt.
takeaways.numbers: hundreds of evals; run tens of thousands of times

takeaways.technique: Adversarial reviewer persona instead of agreeable validator
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately reject the default 'validate the user' behavior and build the agent to reflect patterns back and ask the question underneath the complaint, naming dynamics rather than just feelings.
takeaways.evidence_quote: She does not simply validate. She reflects patterns back. She names dynamics, not just feelings.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before the agent responds to any sensitive message, a background screen checks for clinician-recognized risk patterns; when matched, the agent stops normal coaching and follows a fixed protocol.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Before she ever responds to a sensitive message, she's screening it quietly in the background for the patterns clinicians are trained to recognize.

takeaways.technique: Human dogfooding as a complement to automated evals
takeaways.what_they_do: They run large automated eval batches but insist a human still talks to the agent regularly to feel when tone/behavior drifts, because evals don't cover everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: nothing replaces your gut when emotional context is on the line. So, eat your own dog food. Talk to your agent.

takeaways.technique: Encode a validated domain framework rather than generic helpfulness
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of generic empathy plus tips, the agent's response logic is grounded in two decades-validated clinical frameworks (Gottman, EFT), giving it structured, non-obvious reasoning steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Maxine operates with the Gottman Method and EFT frameworks. That means her response logic is grounded in 40 years of couples research.
